original_question: Let A be a nonnegative tensor of order m and dimension n. Define the majorization matrix by M(A)_{ij} = a_{ij...j}. For a fixed j in [n], call A j-primitive if there exists a positive integer k such that (M(A^k))_{u j} > 0 for every u in [n]. Call A irreducible if there is no nonempty proper subset I of {1, ..., n} such that a_{i_1...i_m} = 0 whenever i_1 is in I and i_2, ..., i_m are all outside I. Is it true that A is primitive if and only if A is irreducible and there exists some j in [n] for which A is j-primitive?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 4.5 in Section 4: the paper asks whether an order-m nonnegative tensor is primitive exactly when it is irreducible and j-primitive for some j, with the proved matrix analogue given just before in Proposition 4.4. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/abs/1408.3457))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target almost exactly: it uses the paper’s majorization matrix M(A)_{ij}=a_{ij...j}, the paper’s notion of j-primitivity via positivity of the j-th column of M(A^k), the standard tensor irreducibility condition used in the paper, and it asks precisely the intended iff characterization. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379515002244?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper restricts the conjecture to tensors of order m>=3; the case m=2 is separated out and proved as Proposition 4.4, so the refined question should not state the tensor conjecture without that restriction. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379515002244?utm_source=openai))

The powers A^k are taken with Shao’s general tensor product, not with an unspecified tensor multiplication. This is an important hidden assumption behind both A^k and M(A^k). ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/abs/1408.3457))

Your draft asks whether A is primitive but does not define primitive. In the paper-faithful stand-alone formulation, one should use Proposition 1.8: A is primitive iff there exists r>=1 such that M(A^r)>0. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379515002244?utm_source=openai))

The ambient parameters should be stated explicitly: m and n are positive integers, n>=2, [n]={1,...,n}, and A is an order-m, dimension-n nonnegative tensor (i.e. with nonnegative entries). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379515002244?utm_source=openai))

The paper presents this as an open conjecture in Section 4, motivated by the matrix characterization in Proposition 4.4, so the rewritten prompt should preserve that status and scope rather than broaden it into a more general tensor-graph or hypergraph problem. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/abs/1408.3457))

No separate homogeneity, polynomial-degree, or nilpotency condition is part of this statement; the only relevant structural restriction here is the tensor order condition m>=3. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379515002244?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: For integers m>=3 and n>=2, let A=(a_{i1...im}) be an order-m, dimension-n tensor with nonnegative real entries, and let A^k denote the k-th power of A under Shao’s general tensor product. Write [n]={1,...,n}, and define the majorization matrix by M(A)_{ij}=a_{ij...j}. Say that A is primitive if there exists r>=1 such that M(A^r)>0; say that A is j-primitive if, for some j in [n], there exists k>=1 such that (M(A^k))_{u j}>0 for every u in [n]; and say that A is irreducible if there is no nonempty proper subset I of [n] such that a_{i1...im}=0 whenever i1 is in I and i2,...,im are all outside I. Is it true that A is primitive if and only if A is irreducible and A is j-primitive for some j in [n]? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379515002244?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the introductory upper-bound conjecture (Conjecture 1.9); it is instead a near-verbatim restatement of the later open problem Conjecture 4.5 in Section 4. The nearby context that makes the question stand alone comes from Definition 2.1 (j-primitivity), Definition 4.3 (irreducibility), Proposition 4.4 (the proved matrix analogue motivating the conjecture), and Proposition 1.8 together with Definition 1.7 and Definition 1.2 (primitive via M(A^r)>0 and powers formed using the general tensor product). Exact page numbers are not exposed in the arXiv/ar5iv HTML view used here; the arXiv abstract page records the submission as a 16-page paper. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/abs/1408.3457))
